name: Rocket Lab
description: Rocket Lab sells access to space and the hardware that goes into it. Its Electron rocket is a small carbon-composite launcher that flew 21 missions in 2025 (the second most frequently launched orbital rocket that year) from a private site in New Zealand and a NASA site in Virginia. A second, larger part of the company builds satellites, satellite components (solar panels, reaction wheels, radios, optical systems) and complete spacecraft, largely through acquisitions such as SolAero, Sinclair Interplanetary, Geost and Motiv. Revenue is two thirds spacecraft and components and one third launches, mostly from US government and commercial satellite operators. It is still losing money (operating loss of $229M in 2025) while it develops Neutron, a larger reusable rocket whose first launch slipped to Q4 2026 after a fuel-tank test failure in January 2026.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code is 3760 (Guided Missiles & Space Vehicles & Parts) from the EDGAR submissions record.

hq.note: EDGAR business address; principal facilities also in Auckland, New Zealand, and the Mahia launch site (FY2025 10-K Item 2)

employees.note: 'Over 2,600 full-time permanent employees worldwide' (FY2025 10-K, Human Capital)

businessLines.name: Space Systems
businessLines.how: Mostly fixed-price and cost-plus contracts to build satellites and buses for governments and prime contractors, recognized as work is done, plus one-time sales of components; flight hardware is on more than 1,800 missions.
businessLines.description: Spacecraft design and manufacture, satellite components (solar, propulsion, avionics, radios), optical systems and on-orbit management; built up by acquisitions (Sinclair 2020, ASI and Planetary Systems 2021, SolAero 2022, Geost Aug 2025, Motiv).

revenue.note: +30% vs FY2024 $310.9M (derived: $402.8M less $91.9M increase); net of a $7.9M downward catch-up adjustment on one contract

businessLines.revenueNote: +30% vs FY2024 $310.9M (derived: $402.8M less $91.9M increase); net of a $7.9M downward catch-up adjustment on one contract

businessLines.name: Launch Services
businessLines.how: A fixed price per launch paid by the satellite owner or government customer, recognized when the mission flies (some over-time recognition on HASTE and select Electron missions); more launches and a higher price per launch drive revenue.
businessLines.description: Electron small orbital rocket (up to about 300 kg to low Earth orbit) and HASTE hypersonic test flights; Neutron medium-lift reusable rocket (about 13,000 kg reusable) in development.

brands.name: Electron
brands.share: 2nd most frequently launched orbital rocket in 2025 (10-K)
